assessment.calibration_basis: p_engine=0.30 already bakes in the harness's conflict-chain clamp [0.3,0.5] for this exact rulebook shape (in-person spree above the prior in-person max, then an online New-device purchase in a never-used region) plus the -0.5 adjustment for the prior cleared same-template alert (CC-1313) and the +0.5 adjustment for a recent card-testing/CNP case on the card; I move slightly up from 0.30 to 0.35, staying inside the required [0.20,0.40] band, because two prior confirmed fraud cases on this same card (CC-3886, CC-0615, both card_not_present_new_device) and the mixed-channel shape of the episode outweigh, but do not erase, the very strong legitimacy signal from the case-memory scorer (cms_p 0.0054 / cal_p 0.0043) and the familiar email/product usage; verdict stays 'uncertain' because probability is well below the 0.70 fraud threshold and the families genuinely conflict (families_fraud=[history], families_legit=[memory]).

evidence.claim: episode_candidates chains four transactions within 48h ending at the flagged one: three in-person product-W purchases in the card's modal region 299.0 on 2016-11-16 (3462385 $440.96, 3462387 $550.03, 3462404 $550.01, only 109-583 seconds apart) reaching a new in-person high for the card, then the flagged online product-R purchase 3464869 for $599.94 roughly 23 hours later.

The flagged transaction 3464869 used device profile Trident/7.0 | Windows 8.1 | ie 11.0 for desktop | 1680x1050 marked New with prior_n=1 (this is its first-ever use on the card) in billing region 327.0, which region_history rates 'rare' with prior_n=1, share 0.0156 and first_ts equal to this same transaction, while home-region activity continued in the surrounding 48h (3 home vs 1 other).

This card carries two prior confirmed-fraud closed cases, CC-3886 (opened 2016-09-24, exposure $175.05) and CC-0615 (opened 2016-07-16, exposure $174.99), both pattern card_not_present_new_device, showing a real precedent for online New-device fraud on this exact card.

The case-memory calibrated score on the flagged transaction is cms_p=0.0054 (cal_p 0.0043), far below fraud-typical levels despite the real-time risk_score of 0.77, and the purchaser email domain anonymous.com had already been used 17 times on this card (prior_pem=17) while product code R is one of the card's usual products (23 prior uses, prior_pcd=23), both consistent with the cardholder's own history.

A prior risk-score alert on this same card, CC-1313 (opened 2016-07-28), was cleared with template cleared_travel and zero exposure, showing the bank has previously found alerts on this card to be legitimate travel/roaming activity rather than fraud.

The New device on the flagged transaction is a strong profile (n_cards_alltime=8, n_cards_30d=4) with zero prior fraud cases attached (n_fraud_cases=0) and device_neighbors shows only this one card active on it in the 30 days before opening, so it is not evidence of a shared fraud ring; a New device alone is not a fraud signal in this dataset.
